She usually does this, which shows she's committed to her son's education. However, last night she didn't help because her son's friend didn't understand the homework.

Is it morally wrong for a parent to not help their child with homework sometimes? I don't think so. Parents can't be available all the time, and it's reasonable to have nights when they can't help. Maybe the parent thought the friend could help, or perhaps she was unavailable because she was helping the friend instead.

I don't see any moral wrongdoing here. The parent is balancing her responsibilities and possibly encouraging her son to seek help from peers, which is a positive thing. So, the action is morally acceptable.
